note: Recorded baselines for the CI regression gate. Measured, not guessed -- a gate
threshold nobody ran is a threshold that fires on noise or never fires at all.
The gate runs on the OFFLINE adapters (HashingEmbedder, ExtractiveGenerator).
That is deliberate: they are deterministic, so a drop is a real regression in
the pipeline rather than model variance, and CI needs no API keys. Numbers that
depend on a provider belong in a keyed nightly run, not in a PR gate.
Recall is deliberately NOT gated. On a five-document corpus with k=8, retrieval
returns nearly everything and recall sits at 1.000 for every configuration --
it cannot detect a regression it is already saturated against. nDCG can, because
it is sensitive to ordering. Recall becomes the headline metric again once the
corpus grows to the ~200 documents docs/05 plans for.

B-dense.gate_rationale: 3% below the recorded baseline, per docs/06 section 4.

B-dense-gemini.note: Not gated -- provider-dependent. Recorded for comparison.

note: Lexical retrieval alone, as a control rather than an ablation arm.
websearch_to_tsquery applies AND semantics over stemmed terms, so a
conversational question ('What transaction throughput did the settlement
platform sustain?') matches nothing and the system correctly declines --
hence over-refusal of 0.90. This does not show lexical search is useless;
it shows it is the wrong tool ALONE for this query distribution. Its value
is exact-term recall (PCI-DSS, CKA, a framework version) that dense
retrieval fumbles, which is why Phase 3 fuses the two rather than choosing.
